database_summary: This is a sales/analytics schema (SQLite) containing dimensional-like lookup tables (countries, products, promotions, channels, times, customers, supplementary_demographics, currency), two fact/event tables for measures (sales, costs) and descriptive attributes. sales is a large transaction/event fact (918,843 rows) recording product/customer/time/channel/promotion level sales. costs is a periodic cost/pricing measurement keyed by product/time/promo/channel (82,112 rows). Dimensions contain mostly stable descriptive attributes; some appear versioned with eff_from/eff_to and valid flags (customers, products). Row counts indicate a star-like shape: many sales rows join to small dimension tables. Currency holds monthly FX rates. Profile values show low-cardinality enums on many dimension columns.

accepted.name: sales_denorm
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  sales.prod_id AS prod_id,
  sales.cust_id AS cust_id,
  sales.time_id AS time_id,
  sales.channel_id AS channel_id,
  sales.promo_id AS promo_id,
  sales.quantity_sold AS quantity_sold,
  sales.amount_sold AS amount_sold,
  products.prod_name AS prod_name,
  products.prod_subcategory AS prod_subcategory,
  products.prod_subcategory_id AS prod_subcategory_id,
  products.prod_category AS prod_category,
  products.prod_category_id AS prod_category_id,
  products.supplier_id AS supplier_id,
  customers.cust_first_name AS cust_first_name,
  customers.cust_last_name AS cust_last_name,
  customers.cust_gender AS cust_gender,
  customers.cust_year_of_birth AS cust_year_of_birth,
  customers.cust_city AS cust_city,
  customers.country_id AS country_id,
  times.calendar_year AS calendar_year,
  times.calendar_month_desc AS calendar_month_desc,
  channels.channel_desc AS channel_desc,
  channels.channel_class AS channel_class,
  promotions.promo_name AS promo_name,
  promotions.promo_category AS promo_category,
  promotions.promo_subcategory AS promo_subcategory
FROM sales
LEFT JOIN products ON sales.prod_id = products.prod_id
LEFT JOIN customers ON sales.cust_id = customers.cust_id
LEFT JOIN times ON sales.time_id = times.time_id
LEFT JOIN channels ON sales.channel_id = channels.channel_id
LEFT JOIN promotions ON sales.promo_id = promotions.promo_id
accepted.description: Denormalized sales transactions joined to core dimensions (products, customers, times, channels, promotions). Use this when analyzing transactions with descriptive attributes from dimensions or when building further aggregates. | Use for: Transaction-level reporting combining product/customer/time/channel/promo attributes; Drilldowns from aggregated metrics to underlying transactions; Filtering transactions by product category, customer demographics, time period, channel or promotion

accepted.name: product_price_cost
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  prod_id AS prod_id,
  time_id AS time_id,
  promo_id AS promo_id,
  channel_id AS channel_id,
  AVG(unit_cost) AS avg_unit_cost,
  AVG(unit_price) AS avg_unit_price,
  MIN(unit_cost) AS min_unit_cost,
  MAX(unit_cost) AS max_unit_cost,
  COUNT(*) AS records_in_costs
FROM costs
GROUP BY
  prod_id,
  time_id,
  promo_id,
  channel_id
accepted.description: Per-product per-time pricing and cost summary from costs table exposing average unit_cost and unit_price and counts of records. Use for margin analysis or joining with sales aggregates. | Use for: Compute average cost/price per product and time period; Join unit cost/price to sales to compute margin; Identify periods or channels with missing or sparse cost records

accepted.name: monthly_sales_by_product
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.prod_id AS prod_id,
  t.calendar_year AS calendar_year,
  t.calendar_month_desc AS calendar_month_desc,
  SUM(s.quantity_sold) AS total_quantity_sold,
  SUM(s.amount_sold) AS total_amount_sold,
  COUNT(*) AS sales_row_count
FROM sales s
JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
GROUP BY
  s.prod_id,
  t.calendar_year,
  t.calendar_month_desc
accepted.description: Monthly aggregated sales measures per product (calendar month), exposing quantity and amount totals. Use for trend analysis, product ranking, and month-over-month calculations. | Use for: Monthly product sales trends; Top products by month (can be combined with a ranking CTE); Month-over-month growth or comparisons

accepted.name: customer_demographics
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  customers.cust_id AS cust_id,
  customers.cust_first_name AS cust_first_name,
  customers.cust_last_name AS cust_last_name,
  customers.cust_gender AS cust_gender,
  customers.cust_year_of_birth AS cust_year_of_birth,
  customers.cust_marital_status AS cust_marital_status,
  customers.cust_city AS cust_city,
  customers.cust_state_province AS cust_state_province,
  customers.country_id AS country_id,
  supplementary_demographics.education AS education,
  supplementary_demographics.occupation AS occupation,
  supplementary_demographics.household_size AS household_size,
  supplementary_demographics.yrs_residence AS yrs_residence,
  supplementary_demographics.affinity_card AS affinity_card,
  supplementary_demographics.cricket AS cricket,
  supplementary_demographics.baseball AS baseball,
  supplementary_demographics.tennis AS tennis,
  supplementary_demographics.soccer AS soccer,
  supplementary_demographics.golf AS golf,
  supplementary_demographics.unknown AS unknown,
  supplementary_demographics.misc AS misc
FROM customers
LEFT JOIN supplementary_demographics ON customers.cust_id = supplementary_demographics.cust_id
accepted.description: Customer records joined with supplementary demographics and country attributes. Use for customer segmentation and demographic-based analyses. | Use for: Customer segmentation by demographics and sports affinities; Joining customer demographics to sales for RFM or lifetime value analyses; Filtering customers by demographic attributes

accepted.name: product_rank_within_month
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.prod_id AS prod_id,
  m.calendar_year AS calendar_year,
  m.calendar_month_desc AS calendar_month_desc,
  m.total_amount_sold AS total_amount_sold,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY m.calendar_year, m.calendar_month_desc ORDER BY m.total_amount_sold DESC) AS month_amount_rank
FROM monthly_sales_by_product m
accepted.description: Per-month rank of products by total_amount_sold, exposing rank and total_amount_sold. Useful for top-N product queries per month when combined with a rank filter. | Use for: Top-N products by revenue within each month; Temporal ranking of products to find movers and shakers; Combining ranks with product attributes to profile top performers

accepted.name: customer_lifetime_sales
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.cust_id AS cust_id,
  COUNT(*) AS purchase_count,
  SUM(s.quantity_sold) AS lifetime_quantity_sold,
  SUM(s.amount_sold) AS lifetime_amount_sold,
  MIN(s.time_id) AS first_purchase_date,
  MAX(s.time_id) AS last_purchase_date
FROM sales s
GROUP BY s.cust_id
accepted.description: Lifetime aggregated sales per customer exposing total quantity and amount purchased and first/last purchase dates. Useful for LTV, retention and cohort analysis. | Use for: Customer lifetime value and recency/frequency analysis; Segmenting customers by purchase activity and recency; Identifying churned vs active customers by last_purchase_date

accepted.name: fx_monthly
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  year AS year,
  month AS month,
  to_us AS to_us,
  printf('%04d-%02d', year, month) AS year_month
FROM currency
accepted.description: Canonical monthly FX rates to USD from currency table, one row per year+month, exposing to_us and a canonical month identifier. Use when normalizing amounts to USD or when joining by year/month. | Use for: Converting local amounts to USD using monthly FX; Joining sales or costs aggregated by month to FX rates
